articles.title: João Diamante leva projeto social ao Rio Gastronomia | G1
articles.standfirst: Criado em 2016, o Diamantes na Cozinha já ajudou a transformar a vida de cerca de 3,5 mil pessoas por meio da formação gratuita em gastronomia.
articles.summary: João Diamante e o projeto Diamantes na Cozinha levam formação gratuita e inclusão ao Rio Gastronomia, impactando 3,5 mil vidas desde 2016.
articles.body:
O chef João Diamante vai comandar um dos restaurantes do Rio Gastronomia, evento que começou esta semana no Jockey Club Brasileiro . Além de participar da programação, ele também vai levar alunos do seu projeto social, o Diamantes na Cozinha , para trabalhar e aproveitar as atrações do festival .

A iniciativa surgiu em 2016 dentro de um projeto social em Vila Isabel. Na época, o curso funcionava com um fogão de 4 bocas e 10 alunos. Hoje, o Diamantes na Cozinha atende jovens e adultos em busca de qualificação profissional e novas oportunidades.

João conta que a ideia nasceu da vontade de retribuir o impacto que projetos sociais tiveram na própria vida.

“Eu fiz parte de diversos projetos sociais — capoeira, jiu-jitsu, balé, dança —, que me fizeram ser quem eu sou hoje. Então eu pensei que, se um dia eu tivesse uma capacidade intelectual bacana, eu gostaria de contribuir de alguma forma e ter um projeto social , só que eu não sabia que ferramenta eu ia utilizar”, afirmou.

João Diamante e seus alunos no curso Diamantes na Cozinha — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Desde 2022, as atividades do projeto acontecem no Hotel Othon Palace, em Copacabana. Segundo o chef executivo do hotel, Rubens Gonçalo, a parceria foi firmada após João procurar um espaço para sediar as aulas.

“O João e eu já nos conhecíamos. Ele veio me falar que estava precisando de uma sede, trouxe o projeto e, de pronto, a gente aceitou, porque está ajudando um projeto social, que é o mais importante”, disse.

Ao longo de 10 anos, o Diamantes na Cozinha já beneficiou cerca de 3.500 pessoas . Uma delas é Ludmilla Dornelles, que afirma ter encontrado uma nova perspectiva de vida após participar do curso.

“Eu estava sentada no meu sofá, ansiosa, deprimida, e o Edimilson Ávila anunciou as inscrições no RJTV. Eu me inscrevi, fui selecionada e fiz o curso. Renovou minha vida. Hoje em dia eu entro em lugares que eu nunca imaginei ”, contou.

Além da capacitação gratuita, alunos do projeto receberam ingressos para o Rio Gastronomia . O evento, que reúne atrações gastronômicas, musicais e culturais, acontece entre os dias 17 de setembro e 4 de outubro .

Para João Diamante, a oportunidade vai além da experiência profissional.

“Os alunos têm essa sede de consumir para além de trabalhar, para além de ser mão de obra. Os alunos vão poder virar consumidores e se divertir também. Normalmente, pessoas que vêm de onde eu venho, favelas e periferias, não têm essa oportunidade”, afirmou.

articles.title: Motorista sobe em teto de carro após ficar ilhado durante enchente | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com a Defesa Civil Estadual, ele foi resgatado pelo Corpo de Bombeiros em Iguape (SP).
articles.summary: De acordo com a Defesa Civil Estadual, ele foi resgatado pelo Corpo de Bombeiros em Iguape (SP).
articles.body:
Homem ficou ilhado em estrada alagada em Iguape — Foto: Defesa Civil SP

Um motorista ficou ilhado em uma estrada alagada de Iguape , no litoral de São Paulo, e precisou subir no teto do carro para escapar da água ( veja acima ). De acordo com a Defesa Civil Estadual, ele foi resgatado pelo Corpo de Bombeiros.

O nível do Rio Ribeira de Iguape subiu cerca de 10 metros acima do normal após as fortes e contínuas chuvas nos estados de São Paulo e Paraná, entre a segunda e terceira semana de setembro. A cheia provocou alagamentos em diversos municípios da região, levando a decretos de emergência em Eldorado, Registro, Ribeira, Iporanga e Barra do Turvo.

Em Iguape, dezenas de famílias precisaram deixar suas casas devido às enchentes . Segundo a Defesa Civil do Estado, foram montados 19 abrigos para desabrigados em seis cidades do Vale do Ribeira.

Apesar do recuo da água, Iguape ainda registra alguns pontos de alagamento e, neste sábado (19), um motorista tentou atravessar uma área alagada na Estrada do Jairê.

De acordo com a Defesa Civil da cidade, moradores informaram que o homem ignorou a orientação para evitar a estrada e acabou preso em meio à inundação. Desta forma, o Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado e, com suporte das equipes da Defesa Civil, retirou a vítima do local.

Ainda segundo o órgão municipal, o carro do motorista também foi removido da estrada.

Cuidados durante o período de reestruturação

A Defesa Civil do Estado mantém equipes mobilizadas no Vale do Ribeira para ajudar na limpeza de ruas e imóveis em Eldorado e Registro. Com apoio de caminhões-pipa, as equipes seguem na região para contribuir para a retomada das áreas afetadas pelas inundações.

Em nota, o órgão informou que, durante a etapa de limpeza, moradores devem estar atentos aos riscos. Confira as orientações:

Utilize botas e luvas para evitar o contato direto com lama e água potencialmente contaminada;

Descarte alimentos que tiveram contato com a água da inundação;

Não volte a ocupar a residência caso suspeite de danos no imóvel. Se houve rachaduras, deformações e outros sinais, é necessário avaliação de um profissional habilitado;

Verifique as instalações elétricas e de gás antes de voltar a utilizá-las.

Segundo a Defesa Civil Estadual, qualquer identificação de sinais de risco deve ser informada ao órgão pelo telefone 199 ou ao Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193.

articles.title: Entenda o que é o sigilo que juiz do TO negou para Alexandre Pires | G1
articles.standfirst: Defesa do cantor alegou risco à privacidade e à exposição de informações patrimoniais. Ação foi movida por empresário que afirma ter sido excluído da negociação.
articles.summary: Defesa do cantor alegou risco à privacidade e à exposição de informações patrimoniais. Ação foi movida por empresário que afirma ter sido excluído da negociação.
articles.body:
O sigilo que a defesa do Alexandre Pires pediu à Justiça era uma solicitação para restringir o acesso público aos autos envolvendo a compra de uma fazenda de R$ 25 milhões pelo cantor, em Dianópolis , no sudeste do Tocantins. O caso entrou em disputa judicial após um sócio alegar que foi excluído da negociação e não recebeu a parte do valor que teria direito.

Na decisão, o juiz entendeu que o interesse público e jornalístico em torno do caso não configura, por si só, violação da privacidade do artista. Com isso, o processo continua acessível, enquanto a ação que discute a venda da propriedade segue em tramitação.

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

A discussão ocorre dentro de uma ação movida pelo empresário Renato Junio Pinto Guimarães, que afirma ter sido excluído da negociação que resultou na venda do Lote 8 da Fazenda Buriti ao cantor. Segundo ele, a propriedade fazia parte de uma sociedade rural formada por três empresários e ele não recebeu a parcela do valor que considera ter direito.

Em nota, o escritório Moraes Advocacia Rural, que representa Renato, afirmou que a ação busca resguardar os direitos patrimoniais do cliente. Segundo a defesa, ele continua aberto ao diálogo e a um acordo entre as partes. O g1 procurou a defesa de Alexandre Pires, mas não recebeu resposta.

Cantor Alexandre Pires — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Foi nesse contexto que a defesa de Alexandre Pires pediu que a tramitação ocorresse em segredo de justiça. O argumento apresentado foi que a exposição do caso poderia atingir a intimidade do artista e revelar informações relacionadas ao seu patrimônio.

Também alegou que os autos contêm materiais considerados sensíveis, como fotografias da residência, vídeos enviados ao Ministério Público e relatos de conflitos pessoais entre os envolvidos.

Ao analisar o pedido, a Justiça rejeitou a adoção de sigilo total. Na decisão, o magistrado afirmou que a repercussão pública do caso e o interesse da imprensa não são suficientes para justificar a restrição completa do acesso aos autos, mas permitiu que cantor peça proteção a documentos específicos considerados sensíveis.

Conflito entre empresários e acionamento do MPTO

A controvérsia envolve a venda de uma área de 1.866 hectares localizada na região do Matopiba. Segundo a defesa de Renato, ele apresentou a propriedade ao cantor antes da conclusão do negócio. Apesar disso, a venda teria sido fechada diretamente entre os outros dois empresários e Alexandre Pires.

Renato acionou a Justiça pedindo a anulação de um terço da venda. Em junho de 2026, o juiz determinou a inclusão de Alexandre Pires no processo por entender que uma eventual decisão sobre a validade do contrato poderia afetar diretamente o imóvel adquirido pelo cantor.

Fazenda fica na região sudeste do Tocantins — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Com o avanço da disputa financeira e judicial, o conflito entre os empresários também envolveu denúncias de violência. Renato anexou ao processo um boletim de ocorrência, fotos e vídeos de episódios de confusão entre as partes.

Em uma gravação feita em julho de 2026, uma caminhonete se aproxima e bate contra o portão de uma fazenda. Em seguida, dois homens descem do veículo, atravessam a cerca e entram na propriedade.

Renato também afirmou que máquinas agrícolas foram retiradas sem autorização e que 11 cabeças de gado foram soltas em direção a uma rodovia. Gabriel e Matheus, por sua vez, afirmam no processo que as máquinas e ferramentas pertenciam exclusivamente a eles e não faziam parte da sociedade.

Diante dos relatos de agressões e de possíveis crimes, a Justiça acionou o Ministério Público do Tocantins (MPTO) em agosto de 2026 para acompanhar e apurar o caso. Uma audiência de conciliação realizada em 27 de agosto terminou sem acordo.

articles.title: Machos de onça-pintada travam batalha sangrenta por fêmea no Pantanal | G1
articles.standfirst: Anambé e Miúdo foram flagrados em confronto diante da fêmea Kwara durante passeio de safari noturno; segundo a Onçafari, disputa por território e fêmeas faz parte do comportamento natural da espécie.
articles.summary: Anambé e Miúdo foram flagrados em confronto diante da fêmea Kwara durante passeio de safari noturno; disputa por território e fêmeas faz parte do comportamento da espécie.
articles.body:
Dois machos de onça-pintada assustaram turistas ao protagonizarem uma briga durante um passeio de safari noturno no Pantanal de Miranda (MS). O confronto foi registrado pela guia e fotógrafa Carol Prange, da ONG Onçafari.

De acordo com a equipe do Onçafari, os machos Anambé e Miúdo foram avistados em uma disputa em frente à fêmea Kwara.

A equipe de campo já havia avistado Anambé e Kwara juntos, mas o macho rosnava em uma direção oposta. Ao iluminar a região, os integrantes da equipe avistaram Miúdo.

Os dois machos passaram a rosnar um para o outro e, em seguida, entraram em confronto. Enquanto isso, Kwara permaneceu escondida na vegetação.

Ao final da disputa, as onças-pintadas ficaram com marcas do confronto, incluindo arranhões e mordidas pelo corpo.

Segundo o Onçafari, Anambé e Miúdo são onças conhecidas pelas câmeras trap desde 2024, mas somente neste ano passaram a ser avistadas em observação direta, após a dispersão de outros dois machos, Timburé e Divino.

“Monitorar esses grandes felinos em vida livre nos proporciona momentos únicos como esse, que nos permitem acompanhar de perto diversos comportamentos naturais, entre eles a disputa por território e por fêmeas”, relatou a equipe nas redes sociais.

Onças-pintadas brigam por fêmea no Pantanal — Foto: Carol Prange/ Onçafari

As vocalizações são uma das formas utilizadas pelas onças-pintadas para se comunicar. O chamado conhecido como esturro pode ser emitido em diferentes tons e ter diferentes funções, como chamar filhotes, afastar competidores ou atrair machos.

Por serem animais territorialistas, as onças também utilizam diferentes estratégias para marcar suas áreas. Entre elas estão fezes, urina, marcas feitas no chão com as patas, conhecidas como scrapes, além de arranhões em árvores.

Os arranhões também podem ser utilizados pelas onças para afiar as garras. Os animais ainda costumam se esfregar em árvores, arbustos e rochas, deixando informações olfativas que podem indicar, por exemplo, a receptividade de uma fêmea para o acasalamento.

De acordo com o Onçafari, as vocalizações também carregam diferentes informações e têm papel importante nas complexas interações sociais entre os indivíduos da espécie.

As onças-pintadas possuem ainda características próprias na forma de caçar. Diferentemente de outros grandes felinos, que geralmente mordem o pescoço das presas para sufocá-las, as onças costumam atacar a região da base do crânio, na parte posterior do pescoço. Elas também podem abater suas presas mordendo o focinho.

O animal é capaz de perseguir e capturar presas em diferentes ambientes, inclusive na terra, na água e em árvores.

articles.title: Vc viu? Gaeco apreende aviões e carros de luxo, falso curso pode ter feito mais de 200 vítimas e criminosos furtam 56 armas no MA | G1
articles.standfirst: Veja quais foram as notícias em destaque ao longo da semana no portal g1 Maranhão.
articles.summary: Veja quais foram as notícias em destaque ao longo da semana no portal g1 Maranhão.
articles.body:
Gaeco apreende aviões e carros de luxo, falso curso pode ter feito mais de 200 vítimas e criminosos furtam 56 armas no MA — Foto: Arte/g1

Confira o resumo de algumas das principais notícias divulgadas pelo g1 Maranhão entre os dias 13 e 19 de setembro.

Jemerson Felipe Rodrigues Pereira começou a sentir falta de ar e tosse poucos dias antes da internação e morreu na madrugada de sexta-feira (11), em Pinheiro, na Baixada Maranhense. — Foto: Divulgação/Redes sociais

O jovem de 28 anos que morreu após aguardar uma transferência hospitalar para São Luís apresentou alterações nos pulmões e o coração aumentado antes de ter o quadro agravado, segundo a família. Jemerson Felipe Rodrigues Pereira começou a sentir falta de ar e tosse poucos dias antes da internação e morreu na madrugada de sexta-feira (11), em Pinheiro , na Baixada Maranhense.

Jemerson Felipe foi sepultado nesse sábado (12), em Bequimão , na Baixada Maranhense, cidade onde nasceu. Familiares e amigos participaram da despedida.

Segundo a família, Jemerson não tinha doenças crônicas e começou a apresentar sintomas respiratórios poucos dias antes da internação. Ele deu entrada no Hospital Municipal Lídia Martins, em Bequimão, com tosse intensa, cansaço e falta de ar.

Um jovem de 18 anos morreu após se afogar na Praia do Caburé, em Barreirinhas, nesse domingo (13). O Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Maranhão (CBMMA) foi acionado por volta das 12h40 e encontrou a vítima inconsciente e sem sinais de respiração. O jovem foi identificado como Carlos Mezaqui Pereira Isidoro.

Segundo os bombeiros, Carlos estava no chão e recebia auxílio de pessoas que estavam no local quando a equipe chegou à praia. Os militares constataram que ele estava em parada cardiorrespiratória e iniciaram manobras de ressuscitação cardiopulmonar (RCP).

Durante o atendimento, a equipe solicitou apoio de uma aeronave do Centro Tático Aéreo (CTA) para transportar a vítima. Segundo o relatório da ocorrência, porém, as aeronaves disponíveis estavam em outras missões e não puderam atender ao chamado.

De acordo com a PM, as agressões começaram após uma festa. O suspeito, identificado como Odair Ferreira Araujo, de 32 anos, teria discutido e agredido física e verbalmente a namorada, de 34 anos, antes de pedir que ela deixasse o local com ele.

Durante o trajeto, ainda segundo a polícia, o homem atacou a mulher com uma faca. Ela foi ferida enquanto tentava se defender, conseguiu fugir e foi encontrada por pessoas que estavam na região.

O Ministério Público do Maranhão (MPMA) deflagrou, nesta terça-feira (15), a Operação Faenerator, que cumpriu mandados de busca e apreensão contra investigados por agiotagem, lavagem de dinheiro, organização criminosa e crimes contra a administração pública.

A operação foi realizada pelo Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate às Organizações Criminosas (Gaeco), por meio do Núcleo Regional de Imperatriz , com apoio da Superintendência Estadual de Investigações Criminais da Polícia Civil (Seic), da Polícia Militar e da Coordenadoria de Assuntos Estratégicos e Inteligência (Caei) do MPMA. A ação foi autorizada pela Vara Especial Colegiada dos Crimes Organizados.

Um homem identificado como Ronaldo dos Santos Oliveira, de 24 anos, investigado por assaltar clientes de bares na Avenida Litorânea, em São Luís, foi preso nessa segunda-feira (14). Segundo a Polícia Civil do Maranhão (PC-MA), ele é suspeito de participar de pelo menos três roubos em estabelecimentos da região.

Segundo a polícia, Ronaldo é o mesmo homem que aparece em imagens de um assalto a um bar na Praia do Calhau, em 23 de agosto. Na ocasião, ele se passou por vendedor ambulante e usou uma caixa de isopor para se aproximar das vítimas e esconder uma arma de fogo. (assista acima).

Ronaldo foi localizado no bairro da Jordoa, em São Luís . Contra ele havia um mandado de prisão temporária. Durante a operação, os policiais também cumpriram um mandado de busca e apreensão em um imóvel relacionado ao investigado.

O influenciador José Segundo relatou ter sido vítima de um assalto nessa terça-feira (15), em uma oficina no bairro São Cristóvão, em São Luís. Segundo ele, um homem armado o rendeu, junto com outras duas pessoas, e efetuou disparos durante a fuga. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Imagens de câmeras de segurança registraram a ação (veja acima). O vídeo mostra o momento em que o suspeito chega de motocicleta, aborda uma das vítimas, que seria o dono do estabelecimento, e aponta a arma para a cabeça dele. Em seguida, José e uma terceira pessoa que estava no local também se rendem.

Na fuga, o homem levou o cordão de ouro do dono estabelecimento e fez disparos na direção das vítimas. Os tiros não atingiram nenhuma das pessoas, mas acertaram o carro do influenciador, que havia acabado de passar por uma reforma. Segundo o influenciador, o suspeito agiu sozinho.

Ex-presidente José Sarney — Foto: Divulgação/Redes sociais

Segundo boletim médico divulgado nesta quarta, Sarney seguirá recebendo acompanhamento de forma ambulatorial, com cuidados domiciliares. A alta ocorre um dia após a equipe médica informar que o ex-presidente apresentava boa evolução clínica.

Sarney estava internado desde domingo (13), após apresentar um quadro de infecção respiratória. Ele foi diagnosticado com pneumonia e permaneceu em tratamento na unidade hospitalar.

Cidade de Buriticupu, no Maranhão. — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Buriticupu

A Justiça determinou, nesta quarta-feira (16), a suspensão imediata de duas portarias de nomeação da Prefeitura de Buriticupu, a pedido do Ministério Público do Maranhão (MPMA). A decisão atende a um pedido da 1ª Promotoria de Justiça da comarca, dentro da execução do Termo de Ajustamento de Conduta (TAC) nº 01/2025, firmado entre o MPMA, o Município e o prefeito João Carlos Teixeira da Silva.

As portarias suspensas nomeavam Gilvan Mascarenhas de Lima para o cargo de assessor especial da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde e Gilberto Mascarenhas de Lima para o cargo de diretor do Departamento de Projetos e Orçamentos da Secretaria Municipal de Infraestrutura, Obras e Urbanismo.

Os dois nomeados são irmãos e já faziam parte do conjunto de fatos acompanhados pelo Ministério Público em procedimentos relacionados ao cumprimento do TAC.

Ele estava acompanhado de um advogado, prestou depoimento e foi liberado porque, naquele momento, não havia mandado de prisão contra ele. A vítima foi morta a tiros na noite da última segunda-feira (14).

Segundo o delegado Fernando Rezende, responsável pelo caso em Paulo Ramos, a Polícia Civil protocolou, nessa quarta um pedido de prisão preventiva contra o suspeito.

O homem preso nesta quinta-feira (17), no Maiobão, em Paço do Lumiar, investigado por oferecer um falso curso de formação marítima, pode ter feito mais de 200 vítimas somente em Arari , segundo a Polícia Civil do Maranhão. Moradores afirmam que pagaram entre R$ 1 mil e R$ 2 mil para garantir uma vaga no curso. Mais de um ano após os primeiros contatos, as aulas ainda não começaram.

A prisão aconteceu após vítimas de Arari denunciarem o caso à Polícia Civil. A partir dos relatos, a Delegacia de Arari passou a investigar Waldenir Duarte Reis por estelionato.

Segundo os moradores, Waldenir chegou ao município se apresentando como tenente aposentado da Marinha e oferecendo um curso de marinheiro mercante, formação voltada para profissionais que atuam em embarcações comerciais.

Moradores do bairro Cidade Olímpica, em São Luís, realizam um protesto na noite desta sexta-feira (18) após a morte de um homem de 24 anos durante uma ocorrência envolvendo policiais militares . De acordo com moradores, a manifestação começou por volta das 14h, após o registro da morte.

O protesto ocorre na Avenida Brasil, uma das principais vias do bairro. Durante a manifestação, moradores bloquearam a pista e atearam fogo em um ônibus. Equipes da Polícia Militar foram enviadas ao local para acompanhar a situação e reforçar a segurança.

A vítima foi identificada por familiares e moradores como Otaniel Francisco Pereira. Segundo os moradores, ele trabalhava em um lava-jato há cerca de sete anos e teria sido atingido enquanto fazia a entrega de uma motocicleta para um cliente.

A Polícia Civil investiga uma denúncia de racismo feita por uma mãe a qual afirma que a filha, uma criança autista, foi chamada de “pretinha” durante uma discussão na praça de alimentação de um shopping, no bairro do Calhau em São Luís. O caso aconteceu na quarta-feira (16), no horário do almoço.

Segundo a Secretaria de Segurança Pública do Maranhão (SSP-MA), o caso está sendo apurado pela Delegacia de Combate aos Crimes Raciais e de Intolerância. As partes envolvidas já prestaram depoimento e, nos próximos dias, testemunhas devem ser ouvidas e imagens das câmeras de segurança do shopping serão requisitadas.

De acordo com a mãe, Pedrolina do Espirito Santo da Silva, conhecida como Keyla Negona, o episódio começou após um desentendimento envolvendo um lugar ocupado na praça de alimentação.

Criminosos furtaram 56 armas de fogo de uma empresa de segurança privada em Bacabal, a cerca de 240 km de São Luís, na noite de sexta-feira (18). O material foi recuperado pela Polícia Militar durante buscas realizadas logo após o crime. Ninguém foi preso.

Segundo informações da PM, equipes foram acionadas depois que o sistema de videomonitoramento da empresa registrou a presença de pessoas dentro das instalações (veja o vídeo acima). Guarnições da Radiopatrulha foram até o endereço e solicitaram apoio da Força Tática.

Com a chegada dos policiais, os criminosos fugiram por áreas próximas à empresa e deixaram parte do material em um matagal localizado nos fundos do imóvel.

articles.summary: Regime iraniano disse ter sido informado de que o governo Trump planeja retomar bombardeios em larga escala contra o território iraniano. Guerra do Oriente Médio está no 7º mês sem perspectiva de ser finalizada.
articles.body:
Mulheres membras da milícia iraniana Basij segurando réplicas de míssil participam de desfile militar em Teerã, no Irã, em 18 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Majid Asgaripour/Wana via REUTERS

O Irã disse neste domingo (20) ter recebido informações de que os Estados Unidos estariam se preparando para retomar os bombardeios contra o Irã e ameaçou retaliar "sem qualquer limitação" contra alvos norte-americanos no Oriente Médio caso isso aconteça.

O alerta veio do Comando Militar Central do regime iraniano após a imprensa dos EUA ter reportado nos últimos dias que o governo Trump estaria se preparando para uma nova escalada contra o Irã na guerra que os dois países travam há mais de seis meses.

"Qualquer ataque dos EUA [contra território iraniano] levará a uma retaliação iraniana sem quaisquer limitações ou considerações contra bases e interesses dos EUA [no Oriente Médio", afirmou o Comando Militar Central iraniano em comunicado.

Teerã disse ainda que essa possível nova escalada seria feita "com o sinal verde de alguns países" do Oriente Médio , e disse ainda que essas nações envolvidas nos ataques dos EUA serão consideradas partes do conflito e "não devem esperar contenção por parte das Forças Armadas iranianas".

Ao mesmo tempo em que há expectativas para uma retomada dos combates em ampla escala, o Irã enviou no sábado aos Estados Unidos uma nova leva de exigências para o fim da guerra no Oriente Médio, em busca de retomar as negociações.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, afirmou neste domingo que está "decidindo se explode o Irã inteiro ou não" e prometeu que "grandes coisas acontecerão em um futuro não tão distante".

articles.title: Itália prepara proibição de burcas e niqabs em escolas e limite de estrangeiros por turma | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Reuters e o portal italiano Il Sole 24 Ore, Giorgia Meloni anunciou a medida durante evento partidário neste domingo (20). A primeira-ministra disse considerar inaceitável que crianças italianas se tornem minoria em suas próprias salas de aula e afirmou que o texto será apresentado em breve ao Conselho de Ministros.
articles.summary: Segundo a Reuters e o portal italiano Il Sole 24 Ore, Giorgia Meloni anunciou a medida durante evento partidário neste domingo (20). A primeira-ministra disse considerar inaceitável que crianças italianas se tornem minoria em suas próprias salas de aula e afirmou que o texto será apresentado em breve ao Conselho de Ministros.
articles.body:
A Itália prepara uma medida para proibir o uso de burcas e niqabs nas escolas e limitar o número de estudantes estrangeiros por turma. O anúncio foi feito pela primeira-ministra Giorgia Meloni neste domingo (20), durante um evento da ala jovem de seu partido, o Irmãos da Itália ( ‘Fratelli d'Italia’ ), em Roma.

Segundo a agência Reuters e o portal italiano Il Sole 24 Ore , a proposta também deve obrigar pais de estudantes estrangeiros que enfrentem dificuldades graves de integração a aprender italiano . Meloni afirmou que a medida será apresentada em breve ao Conselho de Ministros.

A primeira-ministra não informou qual será o número máximo de estudantes estrangeiros permitido por turma.

Quando defendeu a medida, Meloni argumentou que a integração se torna inviável quando muitos estudantes não compreendem o italiano. Segundo ela, se as dificuldades com o idioma afetarem apenas poucas crianças, professores e colegas conseguem ajudá-las. O problema surge quando esses alunos passam a ser muitos ou até a maioria na turma — cenário em que, segundo a primeira-ministra, não há integração, mas sim negligência.

Atualmente, alunos que não têm cidadania italiana representam 11,6% dos matriculados nas escolas do país, segundo a Fondazione ISMU ( ' Iniziative e Studi sulla Multietnicità' ).

Meloni também defendeu a proibição de que estudantes cubram o rosto nas escolas . A medida, segundo ela, está relacionada à igualdade entre homens e mulheres.

“Na escola, você vai com o rosto descoberto, e na Itália ninguém, em nome de uma tradição real ou suposta, pode decidir que uma jovem deve cobrir o rosto. A igualdade entre homens e mulheres é inegociável”, afirmou Meloni, segundo as fontes.

Meloni disse considerar inaceitável que crianças italianas se sintam excluídas ou se tornem minoria dentro da sala de aula. Para ela, estudantes estrangeiros devem “aprender italiano, conhecer a cultura do país e respeitar suas regras”.

A Itália está entre os países europeus mais expostos à chegada de migrantes por causa de sua localização no Mediterrâneo central. A integração de imigrantes, especialmente daqueles vindos de países de maioria muçulmana, é um tema controverso na política e na sociedade.

Durante o mesmo discurso, Meloni anunciou ainda uma mudança na nomenclatura das escolas técnicas e profissionalizantes. O governo pretende aprovar uma lei para que essas instituições também possam usar o termo “liceo”. Segundo Meloni, a mudança pretende reforçar a ideia de que esses estabelecimentos têm o mesmo valor que os demais.

articles.title: Watford artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition
articles.summary: Eric Fawley says that the chance to have his artwork displayed has made him "very happy".
articles.body:
A 94-year-old man with dementia said he was "very happy" to be given the opportunity to have his artwork exhibited in the House of Commons.

Eric Fawley, from Blackpool, has produced hundreds of drawings since arriving at Greenbanks Care Home in Watford, Hertfordshire, over a year ago, after a fire at his home.

His drawings and paintings depict the world around him, as well as his former bosses at BT.

Nirmala Singhvi, the lifestyle coordinator at the home, said: "Eric's story offers a warm and thoughtful look at creativity in later life, as well as the individuality and imagination that remain after a dementia diagnosis."

Fawley's work is due to go on display in the Upper Waiting Hall at the Houses of Parliament in October.

The exhibition was facilitated by the Watford Labour MP Matt Turmaine after he saw Fawley's work at the care home.

Fawley said he began creating artworks from an early age, encouraged by his mother, a violinist, and his father, a gifted amateur painter.

His family were unable to support his ambition to attend art school.

He left school at the age of 14 and worked in a variety of jobs, including electrical work for the famous Blackpool illuminations, before going on to become a Post Office engineer with BT.

Fawley relocated to London, after he married his wife Olive, and he continued to work for the telecoms company.

From there, he rose through the ranks of the company, taking charge of an office where his portraits and keenly observed caricatures of colleagues were prominently displayed.

Fawley said he enjoyed "sending up colleagues" and that they "secretly used to like it".

When drawing someone, he said it was important to start with their hair.

"If the hair is wrong, then everything is wrong," he added.

Since moving to Greenbanks in March last year, Fawley has continued to sketch.

He said being creative helped to focus his mind and "ensures that every day is different".

He has held exhibitions across Essex and also performed a ceremonial ribbon-cutting at an exhibition at Harlow Library.

Staff at the care home are "super proud of him" and are "excited" to see his artwork gain wider recognition, with Fawley challenging perceptions of what people can achieve in care.

articles.title: What are Iran’s latest conditions to end its war with the US?
articles.summary: Iran’s latest stipulations come as growing regional escalation causes oil prices to cross $100 per barrel.
articles.body:
Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei has laid out Tehran’s latest set of conditions to end its war with the United States.

In an exclusive interview with Al Jazeera on Saturday, Rezaei said that Tehran has conveyed its conditions to the US via Qatari mediators, but added that Tehran was more battle-hardened now than in the first 40 days of the war, which began in late February following joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran.

“We will confront America with greater force, and with more numerous and more painful strikes,” said Rezaei.

While full-scale fighting has been paused for months, the two sides are nowhere close to peace. A June 17 60-day memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the US and Iran expired last month. Since then, attacks have risen, especially in and around the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has in effect closed, while the US maintains a blockade of Iran’s southern ports.

Escalating attacks on oil tankers attempting to pass through the strait and the effective Houthi control of the Red Sea route, which Saudi Arabia has been using to export oil, have caused oil prices to cross the $100 mark in recent weeks.

Al Jazeera’s Tohid Asadi, reporting from Tehran, described Rezaei’s remarks as part of the “two-sided, twofold message” Iran has maintained throughout the conflict – combining openness to diplomacy with continued preparations for war.

So what are Iran’s latest conditions, and do they differ from the June MoU?

What are the Iranian conditions to end the war?

An end to the war on all fronts, including, in particular, Lebanon.

The release of its frozen funds that run into billions of US dollars.

An end to the naval blockade on Iranian ports.

An end to US interference in Iran’s internal affairs.

An end to US cooperation with “the opponents of our revolution”.

An end to all US attacks on Iranian territory.

“It is in Washington’s interest to accept these conditions. Trump’s threats will not achieve any results. We are prepared for a decisive war,” said the security chief.

On Sunday morning, Iran’s parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf reiterated Tehran’s stance on the Strait of Hormuz, saying the critical waterway will remain closed until the US fulfils its commitments.

“Until these conditions are met, the legitimate rights of the Iranian nation are recognised, and American commitments are fulfilled, there will be no opening for a return to the previous state of negotiations or for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz,” said Ghalibaf.

Iran’s latest set of conditions bears similarities to its demands under the MoU deal signed in June. That agreement also included an end to the war on all fronts, including in Lebanon; respect for each side’s sovereignty and not meddling in internal affairs; an end to the naval blockade by both sides; and the release of Iran’s frozen funds.

The MoU also called for a $300bn US-backed reconstruction plan, while the two sides also agreed that Iran would not procure or develop nuclear weapons and that Tehran would open the Strait of Hormuz for the safe passage of vessels.

It also required the US to issue waivers for the export of Iranian crude oil and other services, no new sanctions on Iran, and no deployment of additional US forces in the region.

In the interview, Rezaei did not mention war reparations from the US as Tehran has previously demanded.

While there is little genuinely new in the substance of Iranian demands, what has changed is the timing and the channel through which it was delivered, said Adel Abdel Ghafar, a senior fellow focusing on the Middle East at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute.

“With the Islamabad MoU dead and … Rezaei delivering the conditions through Qatar, Iran is putting the onus back on Washington and doing it publicly, for maximum effect,” Abdel Ghafar told Al Jazeera.

Both sides are at an impasse, he explained, with the US able to sustain the naval blockade and hold air superiority but unable to compel capitulation from Iran.

Iran, meanwhile, cannot break the blockade but “keeps enough asymmetric leverage to make things difficult for everyone”, he said.

“Basically Iran is betting [on the] war’s unpopularity and [that the] US midterms [will] shift things in its favour, so it’s going public with demands and putting the ball in Trump’s court.”

Rezaei, in his interview with Al Jazeera, rejected the US accusation that Tehran violated the MoU by striking an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, stating that Iran’s actions came only after US attacks on Bandar Abbas and an Iranian surveillance platform there.

He said any agreement, including the MoU, required recourse to a dispute resolution committee agreed between Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator, and US Vice President JD Vance, which Washington unilaterally withdrew from.

What did Rezaei say on Iran’s nuclear progamme, Yemen and others?

On the nuclear programme, Rezaei said Iran could have withdrawn from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty following attacks by the US and Israel – something that Tehran would not rule out in the future.

“We were indeed threatened, but we have not withdrawn from the treaty to this day,” he said.

For now, however, the country continues to abide by a fatwa (decree) from the former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei banning nuclear weapons, said the security chief.

“But we do not know what will happen in the future,” he said, citing further sanctions or a UN Security Council referral of Iran’s nuclear file as potential future pressure.

On the intensifying war in Yemen, Rezaei denied any Iranian involvement, adding that it could offer mediation between the warring sides. He also said Tehran was not exploiting the conflict “for its own political ends”.

“We are fully prepared to help achieve peace between Yemen and Saudi Arabia,” said Rezaei.

The security chief also dismissed speculation, including inside Iran, that it could close the Bab al-Mandeb strait to pressure global energy markets, stating the waterway “is a Yemeni matter” relating to the Houthi movement and not Iran.

On the Strait of Hormuz, Rezaei said Tehran came within “a short step” of announcing a deal with Oman to manage it, but it may require regional endorsement before being made public.

The US has not yet responded to Iran’s new conditions. Rezaei said Iran is “waiting for the Americans to accept and implement” them.

The US did, however, on Saturday warn its citizens in Iraq, Bahrain, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Qatar, Lebanon, Kuwait and Jordan to exercise “heightened vigilance”, stating that “the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation”.

US President Donald Trump also cut his weekend short from his trip to Camp David, returning to Washington, DC, on Saturday from the secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, the White House said. No explanation was given for the early return, which comes as fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has escalated.

According to Rob Geist Pinfold, a lecturer at King’s College London, Trump may take Iran’s memo seriously – in an effort to end the war before the US midterm elections in November.

“Trump very much wants a deal to wind up the war before the midterms,” Pinfold told Al Jazeera.

“The US’s Gulf allies will also likely push for a renewal of talks. But it doesn’t mean there still aren’t significant substantive gaps between the parties, which make a comprehensive deal unlikely any time soon.”

David Des Roches, a former Pentagon director of Arabian Peninsula affairs, however, told Al Jazeera that Washington was unlikely to see Iran’s terms as a serious opening.

“At first glance, probably not serious; they would be viewed as surrender,” Des Roches said.

But he pointed to Iran’s apparent abandonment of war reparations as a sign of movement.

articles.title: No sugar, no alcohol, no medicines, 300 push-ups and 300 squats: Inside the strict lifestyle of Telegram CEO Pavel Durov
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has spoken openly about the unusual rules he follows around food, exercise, technology and everyday habits. In a conversation.
articles.body: Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has spoken openly about the unusual rules he follows around food, exercise, technology and everyday habits. In a conversation with computer scientist and podcaster Lex Fridman, Durov (41) described a lifestyle built around avoiding several substances, limiting his dependence on his phone, exercising every day and spending quiet time without digital distractions. Durov said he has stayed away from alcohol, tobacco, coffee, pills and illegal drugs for more than 20 years. He also said he does not eat processed sugar, fast food or drink soda, has stopped eating red meat and follows intermittent fasting.“Sugar is pretty easy because it's addictive”When Fridman asked Durov about his diet, he described a fairly restrictive approach. He said he avoids processed sugar, fast food and soda and sometimes follows intermittent fasting, eating only within a six-hour window or sometimes eating only once a day. “Well, sugar is pretty easy because it's addictive. The more sugar you consume, the more you want it, and the hungrier you get,” Durov said. “So, if you want to stay efficient and healthy, why consume processed sugar? You'll just end up snacking all the time.”Durov said intermittent fasting also gives structure to his day and eating habits. “Intermittent fasting, eating only within six hours or not eating for 18 hours every day, also brings structure into your day and into your eating habits. So, you don't crave sugar anymore.” At the same time, he clarified that he is not completely rigid about naturally sweet foods. “Now, I'm not militant about sugar. You can eat berries and fruit if you feel your body needs them. But it's not true to think that it's necessary to consume sweet things, not for children and not for adults.”Durov also said he stopped eating red meat around 20 years ago because of how it made him feel. “Red meat, I stopped eating it about 20 years ago because I just felt heavy every time I had it. So, I guess it's individual.” He explained that he sees it as a personal response to food rather than a universal rule. Instead, he said seafood and vegetables form the basic part of his diet. “So, I normally eat seafood of all kinds and vegetables. This is the basic source of calories for me.”His approach to headaches: “Identify the real cause”Durov also explained why he generally tries to avoid taking medicines. He gave the example of a headache. According to him, taking a painkiller can make the pain disappear without necessarily addressing whatever caused it. “Yes, and trying to identify the real cause of an issue you're experiencing,” he said. “If you're experiencing a headache, one solution would be to take a pill, and then the headache disappears.” He continued: “What this pill would actually do, in most cases, is mute the consequence, your feeling of pain. It's a painkiller.”Durov said people should instead ask themselves what might be behind the problem. “So, you have to ask yourself, ‘What is causing this headache? Do I need to drink some water? Is the air quality here bad? Do I need to start getting more sleep? Is there something wrong with the people around me that are stressing me out?’” “There must be some reason why you're experiencing a headache.”“There are obviously some diseases that you can only fight with antibiotics, for example, so I'm not suggesting we go back to the Middle Ages. But what I'm saying is that we overuse pills,” he added.“My success and health are the result of 20-plus years of discipline"Fridman brought up a statement Durov had previously written about his lifestyle. “If you want to reach your full potential and maintain clarity of mind, stay away from addictive substances. My success and health are the result of 20-plus years of complete abstinence from alcohol, tobacco, coffee, pills, and illegal drugs. Short-term pleasure isn't worth your future.”Asked specifically about alcohol, Durov traced his thinking back to childhood. “When I was 11 years old, my biochemistry teacher gave me a book he had written. It was called The Illusion of Paradise,” he said. According to Durov, the book explained the biological and chemical processes associated with different substances. He said the experience shaped his attitude towards alcohol and other addictive substances.Durov said the book made him think about alcohol in terms of its effects on the brain and long-term consequences. “So think about this. If your brain is the most valuable tool you have on your journey to success and happiness, why would you destroy this tool for short-term pleasure? It sounds ridiculous.”When Fridman asked whether Durov found it difficult to refuse alcohol at parties or social gatherings, he said, “For me, not at all. I've always been ready to stand my ground and say no when I feel something isn't right.”He does not use a phone like most peopleDurov's approach to technology is another unusual part of his routine. Fridman said that during the time he spent with Durov, he barely saw him use a phone in the way most people do, particularly for social media. Durov said, “I don't think a phone is a necessary device.” He recalled growing up without a mobile phone and said he also did not have one when he was a university student. “When I finally got to use a mobile phone, I never used phone calls. I was always in airplane mode or on mute. I hated the idea of being disturbed.”He said he wants to decide for himself what deserves his attention. “My philosophy here is pretty simple. I want to define what is important in my life. I don't want other people or companies, all kinds of organisations, telling me what is important today and what I should be thinking about.”He gives himself time to lie in bed and thinkDurov also said he deliberately tries to allocate as much time as possible for sleep. But he does not necessarily spend all that time sleeping. “Now, even if I allocate, say, 11 or 12 hours for sleep, I won't sleep for 11 or 12 hours. So, what I end up doing is lying in bed thinking.” “Some people hate it. They say, ‘Oh, you have to take a sleeping pill,’ but I never take pills.” “I love these moments. I get so many brilliant ideas, or at least they seem brilliant to me at the moment, while I'm lying in bed, either late in the evening or early in the morning. That's my favourite time of the day.” He said he sometimes gets up and takes a shower without reaching for his phone. “Sometimes I wake up and go take a shower, still without the phone. Beautiful ideas can come to you while you're doing your morning exercise or your morning routine without a phone.”300 push-ups and 300 squats every morningDurov's exercise routine is equally demanding. When Fridman asked about his daily workout, Durov said: “I do 300 push-ups and 300 squats every morning.” That is in addition to his gym routine. “And in addition to that, I normally go to the gym five or six times a week, spending between one and two hours every day.” Durov said the push-ups and squats are not necessarily about changing his body. “I'm not sure they do a lot in terms of changing your body, but they're definitely a good way to practise self-discipline.” He sometimes adds ice baths to the routine for the same reason. “When I can, I also take an ice bath because it's another exercise in self-discipline.” For Durov, discipline is more important than simply building muscle. “I think the main muscle you can exercise is this muscle, the muscle of self-discipline. You know, not your biceps or your pecs or anything else. Because if you train that one, everything else just comes by itself.”Why he likes 'Banya' and cold plungesDurov also spoke about his experience with Banya, a traditional Eastern European steam bath involving intense heat, followed by cold exposure. Fridman, who had accompanied him to a Banya, described Durov as unusually comfortable with the extreme temperatures. Durov said he had simply become accustomed to it. “Banya is this extreme kind of sauna practised by Eastern Europeans. But it is done in a way that maximises heat, and they also use all kinds of herbs and branches. It's a much more holistic and natural experience.”He said the cold plunge is an important part of the experience. “Then, a necessary part of it is that you take a cold plunge and then go back.” Durov acknowledged that the experience can be uncomfortable. He compared the experience with alcohol, describing them as opposite forms of short-term sensation followed, in his view, by different longer-term effects. “In a way, you can look at it as alcohol in reverse. articles.title: A New Jersey couple spent more than 40 years protecting their 90-acre property from development; after ultimately giving away the entire estate, the land is now a free public preserve with a 201-year-old tree
articles.summary: US News: Monmouth County residents have recently received a wonderful gift, one that is going to make the coming autumn a season worth looking forward to. The .
articles.body: Monmouth County residents have recently received a wonderful gift, one that is going to make the coming autumn a season worth looking forward to. The 90-acre Scudder Preserve, in the Navesink section of Middletown, was officially accredited in July as a Level I Arboretum by ArbNet. Among its many treasures are a state-designated 201-year-old tulip tree, rare American chestnuts, immense white oaks and abundant wildlife, all of which the public is welcome to enjoy.The Monmouth Conservation Foundation (MCF), which owns and stewards the preserve, has opened it to the public for free as a community resource for conservation, environmental education and outdoor exploration. “This is easily one of the most unique properties in New Jersey, and provides an outstanding opportunity to learn more about ourselves and our involvement with nature and history,” Tom Dallessio, MCF’s executive director, said.Located at 85 Browns Dock Road, adjacent to Huber Woods, Scudder Preserve contains an extraordinary variety of habitats: mature forests, wetlands and ponds, the bubbling Claypit Creek stream corridor, wildlife-filled meadows, historic buildings and winding nature trails. As an accredited arboretum, the preserve joins an international network dedicated to studying and conserving trees. Connecting Habitats Across NJ has also recognised the property as a valuable core wildlife habitat, identifying essential areas needed to maintain ecological connectivity throughout the state.A legacy of conservationThe preserve's story began more than 40 years ago, when landowners Richard and Elizabeth Scudder strove to protect their property from development. They donated partial conservation easements to the Monmouth Conservation Foundation land trust. By 2012, when Dick passed away, the couple had donated their entire 90 acres to New Jersey Audubon, which in turn gifted the property to MCF in 2024. D&R Greenway Land Trust and MCF now jointly hold the conservation easements, ensuring the land’s long-term ecological integrity. “For more than 40 years, the Scudder family cared for the property with preservation in mind, followed by stewardship by the Audubon Society, before it found a home with MCF. Now Scudder Preserve supports abundant wildlife, established trees, and dynamic, resilient ecosystems. That’s what conservation can do,” Lauren Orme, MCF Communications & Engagement programs manager, said.A living laboratoryThis first land ownership provides a rare opportunity for MCF to restore native plants, improve forest and meadow health, control invasive species, protect water quality and increase the property’s resilience to climate change. MCF also plans to renovate the original Scudder homestead into offices and educational space. Significant funding made this work possible, including a $500,000 grant from the New Jersey Resources Coastal Climate Initiative and a $1 million anonymous donation.In just two years, it has accomplished a lot. A forest stewardship plan is already in place, and a Natural Resource Inventory has documented the property’s plants and trees. Several plant identification signs have been installed, with more to come. Nature trails are being upgraded, and the Rhododendron Trail has been linked to adjacent Huber Woods.MCF is working with Rutgers to incorporate stormwater management by designing bioswales and a native-plant rain garden, which will reduce sediment and nutrient runoff into the pond. MCF also completed an invasive species assessment, with control efforts currently underway.Restoring a historical landscape“It’s incredible to see so many species that you don’t usually see in one place,” said Keith Clayton, MCF’s new stewardship manager. As part of the preserve’s plant identification project, he’s been tagging multiple species to showcase native trees and plants.Clayton emphasised that conservation does not mean erasing the property’s history. “The Scudders loved their ornamental plants, too, and we want to show how you can incorporate natives into beautiful gardens,” he explained.“That balance between history, horticulture and conservation is part of what makes Scudder Preserve special, and MCF can now help create connections for people to the land,” Dallessio said.MCF already offers free conservation programs to the public at the preserve, including evening hikes, guided birdwatching and monarch butterfly tagging with the Field to Flight Foundation. Plenty more programs are on the way.If you can’t make it to the preserve, MCF also brings educational conservation programs directly to the community. Last year its Conservation Van brought programs to more than 3,000 students, with approximately 75% of them in underserved schools. "MCF, working with state, Monmouth County and Middletown Township officials, hopes that Scudder Preserve will provide opportunities for people – especially children – to enjoy, learn about and help protect our natural environment,” said Jack Tassini, MCF Board of Trustees president.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Ukraine targets Russia with over 1,000 drones, killing 2 as Moscow holds last day of elections
articles.summary: Ukraine launched over 1,000 drones and missiles at Moscow in what Russia calls the largest attack of the war, damaging a major oil refinery.
articles.body: Ukraine delivered a barrage of missiles and more than 1,000 drones on Russia, which Moscow is calling the "largest ever" of the war and an attack on its parliamentary elections. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed the strike at the "dollars that support the war machine" as a push for Russia to "end its brutal war and choose peace." "Tonight in the Moscow region, our long-range responses were felt very acutely," Zelenskyy wrote early Sunday morning on X. "One of the key enterprises of the Russian Federation's oil industry and an aggressor's logistics facility have been struck. These are billions of dollars that support the war machine." UKRAINE UNLEASHES MORE THAN 400 DRONES NEAR MOSCOW IN ONE OF WAR'S BIGGEST ATTACKS Zelenskyy added that the Ukraine attack was a stern response to Russian aggression, making a future call for the U.S., Europe and the G7 to deliver "new sanctions." "This week alone, Russia has launched more than 2,000 attack drones against us, most of them jet-powered, as well as 1,700 aerial bombs and 19 missiles of various types," he wrote on X. "Ukraine is constantly looking for and finding ways to defend itself and respond to these attacks on life. "It is important that our partners also look for and find ways to make Russia feel its war. Now is the right moment to take new sanctions steps against the aggressor and force peace through strength. The United States has the means to do this, Europe has them, and so does every G7 country. We are counting on new, strong steps." The Kremlin was wrapping up the third and last day of its parliamentary elections this weekend and said two were killed and 20 wounded, according local Gov. Andrei Vorobyov. UKRAINE LAUNCHES WHAT APPEARS TO BE ONE OF ITS LARGEST DRONE ATTACKS AGAINST RUSSIA: REPORT "The biggest attack by enemy drones has been repelled," Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin wrote on Telegram. "This unprecedented attack was clearly planned with the aim of disrupting the elections. The enemy did not succeed." Russia’s Ministry of Defense said that its forces shot down a total of 1,110 Ukrainian drones across the country, as well as over the peninsula of Crimea and the waters of the Black Sea. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that 450 drones had been destroyed en route to the Russian capital, and that the attack had damaged the Moscow Oil Refinery and a residential building. "Moscow must end its brutal war and choose peace instead of building layered rings of air defense at the expense of other regions," Zelenskyy wrote in a second X post. "Steps toward de-escalation are on the table – in energy and food security. What is needed is political will. I thank everyone who is strengthening Ukraine’s long-range capabilities. I am grateful to everyone who complements our long-range responses with responses through sanctions." Ukraine continued to fend off Russian attacks, according to Zelenskyy. A Russian drone strike hit a monastery in Ukraine’s Kherson region Saturday, killing a member of the clergy and wounding four people, he said. BRINGING THE WAR TO PUTIN’S FRONT DOOR: IS UKRAINE’S ENERGY STRIKE STRATEGY WORKING? A Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv also killed three children and their mother Saturday night, according to Tymur Tkachenko, head of the Kyiv regional state administration. Ukraine's latest drone strikes took place on the final day of Russia’s first wartime parliamentary election — balloting that has been virtually devoid of opposition to President Vladimir Putin’s policies. Russia was also holding the vote in the four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claimed after the war began but still does not fully control, and in Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that Russia invaded in 2014. Putin accused Ukraine of trying to interfere in the election, citing what he said was a Ukrainian strike that killed an election official in her home in the Russian-controlled part of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region Tuesday. articles.title: Israeli settlers storm Al-Aqsa in latest targeting of East Jerusalem sites
articles.summary: Netanyahu storms Western Wall tunnels amid Yom Kippur settler incursions, drawing fierce condemnation.
articles.body:
Israeli settlers have stormed the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in occupied East Jerusalem again and performed Jewish prayers in the courtyard.

The weekend witnessed a series of provocative acts by Israeli politicians and settlers in the build-up to Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, and next month’s Israeli election.

On Thursday, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and others again stormed the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound for Yom Kippur. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also visited a labyrinth of tunnels below occupied East Jerusalem on Saturday.

Early on Sunday morning, Netanyahu released videos and photographs on his official Instagram account documenting his participation in Jewish “Selichot” prayers at the Western Wall, known as the al-Buraq Wall to Muslims.

The tunnels lie underneath occupied East Jerusalem’s bustling Old City and the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound, making the incursions particularly sensitive for the occupied territory’s Palestinian population.

Translation: Happy New Year and a good final signature to all Israelis from the Western Wall.

Under the protection of security forces, Netanyahu, accompanied by several government ministers and thousands of Israeli settlers, made his way onto the plaza of the wall in occupied East Jerusalem on Saturday evening, ahead of Yom Kippur.

Footage shared by the prime minister showed him performing the rituals from behind bulletproof glass. In another video, Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, passed through one of the excavation tunnels running beneath the Western Wall while Jewish prayers took place.

“Well, we are in the tunnels at the al-Buraq Wall. It is moving to touch the rock of our existence. We are here very close to the Holy of Holies. We are here, and we will always remain here,” Netanyahu stated in the video.

Translation: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his wife in prayer for the safety of Israeli soldiers tonight at the Western Wall.

The prime minister’s subterranean visit unfolded alongside a wave of settler incursions into the holy site above ground.

On its official Facebook page, the Palestinian Jerusalem governorate reported that about 570 settlers had stormed the courtyards of the Al-Aqsa Mosque by 10am local time on Sunday. According to the governorate, the settlers performed Talmudic rituals and “epic prostrations” to mark Yom Kippur.

The Palestinian group Hamas strongly condemned the incursions in a press statement published on its official Telegram channel.

“The storming by Benjamin Netanyahu, against whom an arrest warrant has been issued by the International Criminal Court, of the tunnels and excavations beneath the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque and the al-Buraq Wall, and the provocative statements and false claims accompanying it about the so-called Holy of Holies, represents a blatant attack on the identity of the Al-Aqsa Mosque and its status, and a provocation to the feelings of our Palestinian people and the Arab and Islamic nations,” the statement in Arabic said.

The group emphasised Al-Aqsa’s exclusively Islamic heritage and rejected Israel’s ongoing excavations under the holy site.

Israel has been digging beneath occupied East Jerusalem for years, a move that has been condemned by archaeologists and the United Nations. The works are believed to be intended to find proof of the rampart wall of the Second Temple, but experts say there is no proof of this claim . Others view these measures as an attempt by Israel to cement its rule over occupied Palestinian land.

In 2022, Netanyahu led a cabinet meeting in the labyrinth, describing Israel as the “landlords of Jerusalem”. East Jerusalem has been earmarked as the capital of a future Palestinian state by Palestinians.

The timing of Saturday’s visit not only comes on the eve of Yom Kippur but also at a time of huge political significance for the Israeli leader, who trails in the polls against his rival Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party.

Ahmed al-Hila, a political analyst specialising in Middle East affairs and the Arab-Israeli conflict, told Al Jazeera that Netanyahu is using religious symbolism to try to secure his political survival ahead of October’s general election.

“Benjamin Netanyahu wanted, through this visit … creating this symbolism for himself as a leader spearheading the right wing to consolidate the Israeli political and religious narrative in the Al-Aqsa Mosque, to attempt to gather the largest possible number of votes to serve as an electoral lever for him,” said al-Hila.

“As for the intense security mobilisation and Benjamin Netanyahu’s appearance behind a bulletproof glass shield [during a speech above ground], this is a direct indication that this city has not, up to this moment, submitted to Israeli security control, despite the repeated and frequent talk that Jerusalem is ‘the capital of the State of Israel’.”

The visit could also be a message to the wider world, amid global criticism of the controversial illegal settlement project E1, which the Israeli government has issued tenders for, and which appears designed to sever East Jerusalem from the occupied West Bank.

“What further confirms this conclusion is that initiating the settlement project called E1 does not only isolate the northern West Bank from its south … but this settlement project completes the isolation of the city of Jerusalem from its Palestinian surroundings,” Al-Hila said. “Therefore, this visit with its political symbolism confirms the idea of Israeli sovereignty over the city of Jerusalem.”

articles.summary: U.S. ICE agents partnered with the Lee County Sheriff and Florida agencies in a weeklong sweep that netted 500 arrests in Southwest Florida.

Caught in the sweep, according to a statement from ICE, were: a Haitian charged with murder; a Honduran accused of molesting children; a suspected Mexican cartel member; a Guatemalan who allegedly tried to use a Taser on an officer during his arrest; and others with accusations or convictions of crimes such as battery, DUI, hit-and-run, domestic violence, possession of illegal drugs, driving without a license, resisting arrest and returning multiple times to the United States after deportation. GEORGIA ICE SWEEP NABS OVER 700 CRIMINAL ILLEGAL ALIENS, INCLUDING SEX OFFENDERS, CHILD ABUSERS Suspected murderer captured During the operation, the Lee County Sheriff’s Office arrested on a murder charge an illegal alien from Haiti who has been seeking asylum in the United States. ICE LODGES DETAINER FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WITH LENGTHY RAP SHEET AFTER ALLEGED JEALOUSY-FUELED KILLING The medical examiner ruled her death a homicide. ICE ARRESTS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS CONVICTED OF ATTEMPTED MURDER, RAPE AND CHILD SEX CRIMES IN TARGETED CRACKDOWN During the incident, Castro took a trooper’s Taser and attempted to use it against the patrolman, according to ICE. He illegally entered the United States at an unknown time and location without inspection." He "illegally reentered the United States after a previous deportation and has a criminal history that includes driving under the influence, resisting arrest, hit-and-run and public order crimes. articles.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian near Jenin in occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli forces have killed a Palestinian man near Jenin, and an Israeli settler was fatally shot in a separate incident.
articles.body:
Israeli forces have killed a Palestinian man near the city of Jenin in the northern occupied West Bank after he “attempted to carry out a vehicular attack” near an illegal settlement.

An army spokesperson said on Sunday that Israeli forces shot the man near the illegal settlement of Ganim, east of the Palestinian city of Jenin. The spokesperson said there were no casualties among Israeli forces.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society said Israeli forces prevented their medical team from reaching the victim, the Wafa news agency reported.

In a separate incident, an Israeli settler was fatally shot in an attack near the illegal settlement of Halamish in the central West Bank.

The 30-year-old man was taken to a hospital where he died of his wounds, police said.

The military said it the suspect opened fire from a vehicle and left the scene on foot. After a search by security forces, the military said the man, who was injured while fleeing, was detained at a hospital where he had sought care.

Israel’s National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir demanded on Sunday that the suspect face the death penalty. He said in a post on X that this is the “first case that meets the criteria of the Death Penalty Law” since the Knesset – Israel’s parliament – adopted the law in March this year.

The death penalty law allows military courts to impose the death penalty on Palestinians convicted of killing Israelis, but does not impose the same penalty on Israelis convicted of killing Palestinians.

Ben-Gvir was a strident campaigner for the law before it was adopted. In May, he shared an AI-generated video on TikTok, saying he “dreams” of nooses .

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he ordered the military and security agencies to increase their forces and carry out arrests and offensive ⁠activities in the area. He also said he ordered the demolition of the suspected attacker’s home.

After the shooting, Israeli forces closed all entry and exit points to Ramallah and el-Bireh cities, Wafa reported.

Israeli violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has been steadily growing since the eruption of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, but the pogroms intensified significantly this year.

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) recorded more than 1,330 settler-related attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank from January to late July, averaging six a day and marking the fastest pace in about 20 years.

Various settler groups , often supported or protected by Israeli soldiers, have attacked Palestinians in several ways, including shootings, besieging homes and engaging in other forms of communal violence that experts have described as “ pogroms “.

In July, Israeli forces shot dead four Palestinians in the town of Tal, near Nablus, during a settler incursion on their land. Two Israelis were also killed in the incident, which triggered a violent “ rampage ” by Israeli settlers.

Rights groups warn that settlers are increasingly armed with military-issued weaponry and wear military uniforms during attacks, blurring the line between settler and soldier.

articles.title: Lib Dems sleepwalking to irrelevance under Davey, says council leader
articles.summary: Devon County Council leader Julian Brazil tells the BBC Ed Davey is not the right person to lead the party.
articles.body:
A Liberal Democrat council leader has said the party is "sleepwalking into irrelevance" and questioned whether Sir Ed Davey was the right leader.

Julian Brazil, the leader of Devon County Council, told the BBC the party was "lacking ambition" and "not saying the things that people can relate to".

Asked whether Sir Ed was the right leader for the party, Brazil said "I wish he was" but "all the evidence is no".

A Lib Dem spokesperson said the party was in "an incredibly strong position" under Sir Ed's leadership because he was focused on the "issues that really matter" such as the cost of living and the health service.

"Under Ed's leadership we had our best result for a century, and achieved a record breaking streak of remarkable local election results," they added.

"We are the most united party in Westminster and with Ed as leader we will stop Reform and the Conservatives and change our country after a decade of failing governments."

Sir Ed led the party to record 72 MPs in the 2024 general election, but it has slipped to fourth or fifth in national opinion polls, behind the Greens and Reform UK.

Brazil told the BBC the Lib Dems had "allowed other parties to go steaming past us," adding that "something has to change within the party if we're going to move to the next level and it's not happening at the moment".

He added: "I think there is a fantastic opportunity now for us to be right in the middle of politics and we don't seem to be. We seem to be peripheral.

"We're lacking ambition, we're lacking courage of our convictions. We're not saying the things that people can relate to."

He said the party was asking people to "vote for us because we're not somebody else".

Brazil became the leader of Devon County Council in May last year after the Lib Dems overtook the Tories to become the largest party, but without overall control.

His comments are echoed privately by some Lib Dem MPs, as they gather for their annual conference in Brighton.

In an essay, written ahead of the conference, South Cotswolds MP Roz Savage asked: "Why are we as a party struggling for relevance at precisely the moment when so many people feel powerless?"

She urged the party to rediscover its "insurgent spirit" rather than being the "polite custodians of a system that leaves people feeling powerless".

Sir Ed, who was elected leader in 2020, told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg he shared the "frustration" of some of his MPs that they could not bring about "real change," blaming the UK's political system.

But he insisted the party was gaining ground in council elections.

"It's the most successful period that we've had," he said.

"But outside elections, in terms of changing the law, which is what my MPs rightly want to do, and they're a very talented bunch, and they've actually had more success than all the other smaller parties, but they want to have more."

Sir Ed was asked directly about Brazil's complaints during a conference Q+A session on Sunday.

"I have know Julian for many years and he is good councillor," he said.

"In Devon the party doing better than it has for decades - six MPs and local councils all across the area and in parts of Devon we are showing how to beat Reform.

"I'm really proud of what we have been doing in Devon."

Sir Ed got a vote of confidence from former coalition cabinet colleague Sir Vince Cable, who told a fringe meeting that he was the most successful leader in the party's history and "you can't argue with success".

Speaking at another fringe meeting, pollster Luke Tryl said the Lib Dems were not cutting through nationally and needed a more compelling message.

The executive director of More in Common said it was possible the party could take more seats in traditional Tory heartlands at the next election, potentially putting Sir Ed in a position to be deputy prime minister in a Labour-led government.

But the risk for the party, he added, was the Tories saying "if you vote Lib Dem you will get Labour".

articles.title: Southampton man rearrested after missing mum's remains found
articles.summary: The remains of mother-of-three Joanne Sheen were found almost seven years after she went missing.
articles.body:
A 56-year-old man has been rearrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit murder and further arrested on suspicion of murder after human remains were identified as a missing mother-of-three.

Joanne Sheen, then aged 44, was last seen when she travelled from Fareham to Southampton with a friend on 5 December 2019.

Metropolitan Police officers were called to Padstow Walk in Feltham, London, on 12 August after bones were found in shrubland damaged by a fire a week earlier.

The man, from Southampton, first arrested in 2020, has been released on conditional bail. Another man, also 56 and from Southampton, was released on bail after being arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit murder.

Sheen's disappearance sparked a major police investigation, which the force said led to more than 4,000 lines of inquiry, more than 300 statements taken and searches of more than 10 addresses and numerous water vessels.

Sheen was reported missing by her family in February 2020, two months after she was last seen.

An investigation led to a number of arrests on suspicion of conspiracy to murder in 2020, but no-one was charged and the case remained unsolved.

Officers previously said she had no fixed address and did not own a vehicle or hold a bank account.

London Fire Brigade attended a fire at Bedfont Pits on 5 August that damaged about two hectares of shrubland.

The Metropolitan Police said human remains were found by a member of the public at the site near Bedfont Lakes Country Park a week later.

Detectives in London handed the investigation over to Hampshire Police after the remains were identified as those of Sheen.
